findings.description:
ICE PACK TEST

INDICATION: Evaluation of left ptosis.

TECHNIQUE: Crushed ice in a surgical glove applied over the closed left upper eyelid for 2 minutes. Marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) measured immediately before and after application.

RESULTS:
  Left MRD1 before application: 1.5 mm.
  Left MRD1 after application (2 minutes): 4.0 mm.
  Improvement: 2.5 mm.

IMPRESSION: Positive ice pack test (improvement in ptosis of at least 2 mm after cooling). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Positive ice pack test: left MRD1 improved from 1.5 mm to 4.0 mm (2.5 mm) after 2 minutes of cooling

findings.description:
BEDSIDE RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTING

INDICATION: Generalized fatigable weakness with bulbar symptoms; baseline respiratory muscle strength.

MEASUREMENTS (seated; weight 65.4 kg, height 163 cm):
  FVC: 3.62 L (predicted 3.55 L; 102% predicted; 55 mL/kg)
  MIP (NIF): -72 cmH2O (lower limit of normal for age and sex about -60 cmH2O)
  MEP: 88 cmH2O (lower limit of normal about 80 cmH2O)
  Single-breath count: 38
  Cough: strong

IMPRESSION: FVC, MIP and MEP within the predicted range. Clinical correlation recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 8.7 nmol/L (reference <= 0.02) with blocking 62% and modulating 78%; TSH 2.2 and free T4 normal on levothyroxine; TRAb negative; anti-TPO 62 IU/mL
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function with thyroid antibodies
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable ptosis, diplopia, jaw fatigue and proximal weakness: AChR binding antibody (RIA or cell-based assay) first; thyroid function and antibodies because she has treated Graves disease and the ophthalmologist raised thyroid eye disease (Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019; Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3 Hz decrement in orbicularis oculi 20%, deltoid 15% and masseter 24% with normal baseline CMAPs and no post-exercise facilitation (4%)
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz in facial, masticatory and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: Low-rate RNS of the weak facial, masseter and deltoid muscles documents the postsynaptic decrement; brief exercise testing excludes presynaptic facilitation (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Frontalis mean MCD 82 microseconds with increased jitter in 17 of 20 pairs and blocking in 8
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG (not needed once RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: SFEMG is reserved for a normal RNS or seronegative disease; with high AChR titres and a clear decrement it adds nothing to the diagnosis (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves from 1.5 to 4.0 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Bedside ice pack test of the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable left ptosis in a patient whose ophthalmologist suspects thyroid eye disease: an MRD1 improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling supports a neuromuscular junction cause at the bedside.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No anterior mediastinal mass; residual thymic tissue appropriate for age; no thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the mediastinum for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Mediastinal imaging is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025); without thymoma she is a candidate for thymectomy under the MGTX criteria.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 3.62 L (102% predicted, 55 mL/kg), MIP -72 cmH2O, MEP 88 cmH2O: no respiratory compromise
action_criteria.label: Measure FVC, MIP and MEP as a respiratory baseline
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar symptoms (jaw fatigue, nasal speech) and neck flexor weakness: FVC in mL/kg, MIP and MEP give the baseline before immunotherapy and thymectomy (20/30/40 rule, Lawn, Arch Neurol 2001).

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to thyroid eye disease, allergy or stress before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
Do not prescribe mycophenolate or methotrexate without effective contraception and pregnancy counselling.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily and titrate to 60 mg four to five times daily according to response and muscarinic side effects

Start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase gradually with monitoring of bulbar and respiratory function for early steroid-induced worsening; add a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term steroids are needed

Refer for elective thymectomy once symptoms are controlled: thymectomy is recommended for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65 (MGTX); give IVIG or plasma exchange before surgery if bulbar weakness persists

Counsel on pregnancy planning: pyridostigmine, prednisone and azathioprine are acceptable in pregnancy, mycophenolate and methotrexate are teratogenic and need effective contraception and a washout before conception, and a future pregnancy needs joint neurology and obstetric care
Keep her euthyroid on levothyroxine with periodic TSH and free T4, since both hypothyroidism and over-replacement can aggravate MG weakness
Give her a list of drugs that can worsen MG and check every new prescription against it

avoided_actions.rationale: MG is a disorder of the neuromuscular junction; EEG has no diagnostic role (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG and nothing in this presentation raises Miller Fisher syndrome or a CNS cause (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
FDG-PET has no role in MG; mediastinal CT answers the thymoma question (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

Brain and orbit MRI is reserved for negative serology and neurophysiology or a central or orbital mimic; here AChR antibodies and RNS are positive, the orbits are clinically quiet and TRAb is negative (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac symptom or sign; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
Regular rhythm, euthyroid on replacement and no palpitations; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), AChR antibody-positive, without thymoma; concurrent post-Graves autoimmune thyroid disease (now hypothyroid on levothyroxine)

differential.key_features: No proptosis, lid retraction or inflammatory signs (clinical activity score 0/7) and TRAb negative; ptosis is fatigable and improves with ice, which thyroid eye disease does not do; AChR antibodies and a decrement establish MG.
TSH 2.2 and free T4 normal on levothyroxine, so there is no over-replacement; thyroid myopathy does not cause fatigable ptosis or an RNS decrement.
Normal baseline CMAPs, a 3 Hz decrement and no post-exercise facilitation (4%), preserved reflexes, prominent ocular signs; AChR binding antibody strongly positive.
Markedly elevated AChR antibodies establish organic pathology.

key_clinical_evidence: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with diurnal pattern (worse evening) is the clinical hallmark of MG — fixed weakness suggests an alternative diagnosis.
Ocular involvement (ptosis, diplopia) is asymmetric and fatigable in MG; thyroid eye disease causes restrictive (not fatigable) ophthalmoplegia.
A high AChR binding titre (8.7 nmol/L) with a 15-24% decrement on 3 Hz RNS establishes generalized AChR-positive MG; SFEMG is not needed.

Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma; here it is normal, and thymectomy is still recommended under MGTX for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
Fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium and neuromuscular blockers can worsen MG and must be checked against every new prescription.
Post-Graves autoimmune background increases MG risk (polyautoimmunity); recognize this co-occurrence rather than re-attribute MG symptoms to thyroid disease.
Childbearing-age woman: address contraception and pre-pregnancy MG management early.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Graves orbitopathy is restrictive and gives proptosis/lid retraction; this is fatigable and AChR-antibody positive — independent MG.
red_herrings.data_point: Treated Graves disease, now hypothyroid on levothyroxine
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute ocular symptoms to residual Graves orbitopathy.

sequence_constraints.reason: Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).

patient.chief_complaint: Left eyelid drooping with double vision and jaw fatigue for 8 weeks

past_medical_history: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Graves disease treated with radioiodine 2 years ago, now hypothyroid on levothyroxine)

patient.history_present_illness: A 29-year-old woman with a history of Graves disease treated with radioiodine (now hypothyroid on levothyroxine) presented with 8 weeks of left eyelid drooping, double vision, and jaw fatigue. She first noticed her left eyelid drooping while studying late at night approximately 8 weeks ago. Initially she thought it was related to sleep deprivation from graduate school deadlines. However, the ptosis persisted during the day and worsened in the afternoon. She started experiencing double vision approximately 6 weeks ago — she described seeing two images side by side when looking to the right, and vertical separation of images when looking up. She noticed that her jaw became very fatigued when eating — by the third or fourth bite of a tough food she needed to rest her jaw for 30 seconds before continuing. Her speech became noticeably nasal after she had been speaking for more than a few minutes. She denied any difficulty swallowing liquids or solids but acknowledged food 'sometimes takes longer to chew.' She has had no headache, no limb numbness or tingling, no falls, no bowel or bladder symptoms. She initially saw a student health clinic who attributed the ptosis to allergic conjunctivitis and treated her with antihistamine eye drops without improvement. She subsequently saw an ophthalmologist who ruled out structural eyelid pathology and confirmed no proptosis — noting her prior Graves disease history, the ophthalmologist was concerned about reactivation of thyroid eye disease and referred her to neurology. Her family history includes thyroid disease and she had a recent flare of anxiety attributed to her graduate school stress, for which she declined medication.

neurological_exam.additional: Nasal voice quality after sustained speech. Difficulty chewing — jaw fatigues after 2-3 minutes eating. No respiratory distress.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left ptosis, MRD1 1.5 mm (right 3.5 mm). Complete fatigable ptosis left eye on sustained upgaze at 35 seconds. Right ptosis mild intermittent. Limited adduction of the left eye with horizontal diplopia on rightward gaze; vertical diplopia on upgaze. Pupils equal, reactive. Bilateral mild facial weakness — patient unable to close eyes tightly against resistance. No proptosis, lid retraction, chemosis or eyelid oedema (clinical activity score 0/7).
neurological_exam.gait: Normal. Mildly waddling after walking one block.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Normal cognition and language.
neurological_exam.motor: Shoulder abductors 4/5 bilaterally. Hip flexors 4+/5. Neck flexors 4-/5. Distal strength 5/5. Fatigability: neck flexion fails after 30 seconds sustained effort.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs.
physical_exam.general: Alert, well-appearing young woman; left ptosis. Weight 65.4 kg, height 163 cm.
physical_exam.respiratory: Clear to auscultation; no accessory muscle use; SpO2 99% on room air.
